input.description: Read the shared ASD MFA policy helper

result.output:
function Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the enabled Conditional Access policies that require MFA for the given scope, for the ASD checks.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Shared by the Essential Eight multi-factor authentication checks. A policy counts when it is enabled,
    targets all cloud apps, targets the scope (all users, or every privileged directory role) and grants
    access only with multi-factor authentication, or with a phishing-resistant authentication strength when
    -PhishingResistant is given. Policies that only act on Identity Protection risk are left out, because they
    do not require MFA on every sign-in.
    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy -Scope AllUsers
    Returns the policies that require MFA for all users on all cloud apps.
    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy -Scope PrivilegedRoles -PhishingResistant
    Returns the policies that require a phishing-resistant authentication strength for every privileged role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param(
        # Who the policy must cover: every user, or every privileged directory role.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateSet('AllUsers', 'PrivilegedRoles')]
        [string] $Scope,
        # Require a phishing-resistant authentication strength instead of any MFA.
        [switch] $PhishingResistant
    )
    # The built-in phishing-resistant strength, and the combinations a custom strength may be limited to.
    $phishingResistantStrengthId = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004'
    $phishingResistantCombinations = @('windowsHelloForBusiness', 'fido2', 'x509CertificateMultiFactor')
    # The fourteen roles of Microsoft's 'Require MFA for administrators' Conditional Access template, by role
    # template ID; the same set MT.1006 checks.
    $privilegedRoleIds = @(
        '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10', # Global Administrator
        'e8611ab8-c189-46e8-94e1-60213ab1f814', # Privileged Role Administrator
        '7be44c8a-adaf-4e2a-84d6-ab2649e08a13', # Privileged Authentication Administrator
        '194ae4cb-b126-40b2-bd5b-6091b380977d', # Security Administrator
        'fe930be7-5e62-47db-91af-98c3a49a38b1', # User Administrator
        '9b895d92-2cd3-44c7-9d02-a6ac2d5ea5c3', # Application Administrator
        '158c047a-c907-4556-b7ef-446551a6b5f7', # Cloud Application Administrator
        'b1be1c3e-b65d-4f19-8427-f6fa0d97feb9', # Conditional Access Administrator
        '29232cdf-9323-42fd-ade2-1d097af3e4de', # Exchange Administrator
        'f28a1f50-f6e7-4571-818b-6a12f2af6b6c', # SharePoint Administrator
        'c4e39bd9-1100-46d3-8c65-fb160da0071f', # Authentication Administrator
        '966707d0-3269-4727-9be2-8c3a10f19b9d', # Password Administrator
        'b0f54661-2d74-4c50-afa3-1ec803f12efe', # Billing Administrator
        '729827e3-9c14-49f7-bb1b-9608f156bbb8'  # Helpdesk Administrator
    )
    $policies = @(Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object {
            $_.state -eq 'enabled' -and
            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -notcontains 'passwordChange' -and
            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -notcontains 'riskRemediation' -and
            -not $_.conditions.userRiskLevels -and
            -not $_.conditions.signInRiskLevels
        })
    foreach ($policy in $policies) {
        if ($policy.conditions.applications.includeApplications -notcontains 'All') { continue }
        $users = $policy.conditions.users
        $coversScope = switch ($Scope) {
            'AllUsers' { $users.includeUsers -contains 'All' }
            'PrivilegedRoles' {
                $users.includeUsers -contains 'All' -or
                @($privilegedRoleIds | Where-Object { $_ -notin $users.includeRoles -or $_ -in $users.excludeRoles }).Count -eq 0
            }
        }
        if (-not $coversScope) { continue }
        # As in MT.1006 and MT.1007, a grant that lists MFA counts even when the operator is OR.
        $grant = $policy.grantControls
        $strength = $grant.authenticationStrength
        $requiresMfa = if ($PhishingResistant) {
            $strength -and (
                $strength.id -eq $phishingResistantStrengthId -or
                ($strength.allowedCombinations -and @($strength.allowedCombinations | Where-Object { $_ -notin $phishingResistantCombinations }).Count -eq 0)
            )
        } else {
            $grant.builtInControls -contains 'mfa' -or $strength.requirementsSatisfied -contains 'mfa'
        }
        if ($requiresMfa) { $policy }
    }
}

content.text:
The next one is **[#2552](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2552)** from jusso-dev. It adds a new built-in suite, `tests/asd`, for the ASD Essential Eight and the Australian Information Security Manual (ISM): two framework files and 15 checks across Entra and Intune. Nobody has reviewed it yet. The only other open PRs are contributors' drafts and #2598, the docs bot's routine refresh, which needs nothing from us.

**What's good:**
- **The suite follows the repo's design.** It has `suite.json`, `frameworks/essential-eight.json` and `frameworks/ism.json`, with checks named after the ISM control they implement (`Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`, which brings `ism:ISM-1504` along with it).
- **The framework files follow the hard rule.** They hold only IDs and facts (level, strategy, guideline, applicability) with no control text, and include CC BY 4.0 attribution. A script, `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`, generates them from ASD's published machine-readable catalogue (OSCAL).
- **The logic I spot-checked is sound.**
  - The shared MFA helper matches how MT.1006 and MT.1007 work.
  - ISM-1648 (privileged users inactive for 45 days) counts PIM-eligible admins as well as active ones, and leaves out emergency access accounts.
- **Two CIS tests gain Essential Eight mappings.** It adds `essential-eight:ISM-1649` to CIS 5.3.1 and `essential-eight:ISM-1647` to CIS 5.3.3.

**What needs fixing:**
1. **Merge conflicts in three files.**
   - Two are the generated Claude copies, `.claude/agents/maester-test-expert.md` and `.claude/skills/.../SKILL.md`, which can be regenerated.
   - The third is the expected counts in `Frameworks.Tests.ps1`.
   - Because of the conflict, build validation hasn't run on this PR at all.
2. **A generated file was edited by hand.** `website/docs/commands/Invoke-Maester.mdx` is generated from the command's help. The PR also updates that help, so the docs bot will produce the same change.
3. **Attribute review fails on ASD.ISM-1648.** The bot expects Severity Medium (it's a second layer behind MFA, and the rubric picks the lower level when two fit) and ImplementationCost Medium (each account needs its owner's input, plus a PIM alert or access review). I agree with both.
4. **No `suite: asd` label exists yet.** It needs adding to `.github/labels.json` and the triage skill, as we did for `product: fabric`.

**Minor:**
- `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` counts only users who hold a role directly, so members of role-assignable groups are missed.
- The MFA helper doesn't look at platform, location or client-app conditions, so a policy limited to one platform still counts. MT.1006 does the same.

**Your call:** this adds a new built-in suite and reserves the `ASD.` prefix, which means maintaining two more frameworks long term. I'd accept it, given how closely it follows the CIS and CISA pattern.
it has cmdlets with the name asd in it, and some of the code might be duplicates of other tests. we should think of re-using if they are identical... can you review with that lens?
I'll compare each ASD helper and check with what already exists in Maester.

content.text:
You're right: a good part of [#2552](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2552) re-implements things Maester already has. Here's what I found.

## Helpers named after the suite

`Test-MtAsd*` for the test functions themselves is fine; it matches `Test-MtCis*` and `Test-MtCisa*`. The problem is the shared helpers. AGENTS.md says to "put a function by its job, not by the check that first needed it", and three of these four have a general job:

| ASD helper | What already exists | Suggestion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` (`checks/asd/entra`) | `Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem` and `…GrantProblem` (`checks/cis/entra`), used by CIS 5.2.2.x. They also flag policies narrowed by platform, location or client app, which the ASD helper ignores. | Move the CIS pair to `internal/services/entra/`, renamed without "Cis", and have both suites use it. Drop `Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy`. |
| Hard-coded list of 14 admin role IDs inside that helper | `Get-MtCisAdministratorRole` (15 roles) and `Get-MtRole -CisaHighlyPrivilegedRoles` | Use one list. A third, slightly different one would drift. |
| `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` | `Get-MtRoleMember` (public), which returns active and eligible members and expands groups | Use `Get-MtRoleMember`. The ASD helper misses admins who get their role through a role-assignable group. |
| `Test-MtAsdAsrRule` (`checks/asd/intune`) | MT.1178 parses the same Intune ASR settings, but inline, with no helper | Keep it, but move it to `internal/services/intune/` with a general name (for example `Get-MtIntuneAsrRuleState`). Switching MT.1178 to it can be a follow-up. |
| `Get-MtIntuneConfigurationPolicySetting` | Nothing equivalent | Already in the right place (`services/intune`). Keep it. |

## Checks that read a setting another test already reads

| ASD check | Existing test | Overlap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ISM-1504 MFA for all users | CIS 5.2.2.2, MT.1007 | Same policy check |
| ISM-1173 MFA for admins | CIS 5.2.2.1, MT.1006 | Same check, with a different role list (14 roles vs 15) |
| ISM-1872 phishing-resistant MFA for all users | CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 | The PR even maps `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` onto it. The logic differs: CISA matches the strength by display name, ASD by ID or allowed methods. |
| ISM-1649 no permanent admin assignments | CIS 5.3.1 | The PR also adds `essential-eight:ISM-1649` to CIS 5.3.1, so **two tests now implement ISM-1649 with different rules**. CIS 5.3.1 fails any active assignment; ASD only fails permanent ones. |
| ISM-1403 smart lockout ≤ 5 | CIS 5.2.3.8 (≤ 10), EIDSCA.PR06 | **Three implementations of one setting.** ASD reads `settings` and CIS reads `groupSettings`. |
| ISM-1648 inactive privileged users | none (MT.1206 is about agent identities) | New |

The rubric says the same check in two suites gets the same attribute values. These overlaps would also put several tests' results on the same setting, and in two cases they could disagree.

The other 9 checks are new to Maester, and I found no equivalents: ISM-0445, ISM-1648, the macro and IE checks (1488, 1654, 1672), the four ASR rules (1667, 1668, 1669, 1673) and the update-ring deadline (1695).

## How I'd fix it

1. **One test per setting.** For the 6 overlaps, either:
   - keep the ASD tests but have each call the shared helper, so they can't disagree and share attribute values; or
   - drop the ASD test and add `essential-eight:ISM-xxxx` to the existing test's `Control`, as the PR already does for CIS 5.3.1.

   The second fits AGENTS.md ("any other test may name the same requirements") and gives 6 fewer tests to maintain. The cost is that an ASD-only run (`-Suite ASD`) wouldn't include those checks.
2. **Fix the helpers** as in the table above.
3. **The earlier fixes:** the three merge conflicts, the hand-edited `Invoke-Maester.mdx`, the ISM-1648 Severity and ImplementationCost values, and a `suite: asd` label.

On step 1, I'd keep the ASD tests that are true duplicates (1504, 1173, 1872) but have them call the shared helpers. That way the Essential Eight report still works on its own. For ISM-1649 and ISM-1403, which differ from their CIS counterparts, the shared helper should take a parameter so each benchmark's own rule still applies (CIS ≤ 10 vs ISM ≤ 5).

﻿function Test-MtAsdMfaAllUsers {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1504 (Essential Eight, Multi-factor authentication, Maturity Level One) asks that multi-factor
    authentication is used to authenticate users to the organisation's online services that process, store or
    communicate its sensitive data. ISM-0974 (Maturity Level Two) extends it to unprivileged users of systems.

    The check passes when at least one enabled Conditional Access policy targets all users and all cloud apps
    and grants access only with the built-in MFA control or an authentication strength that satisfies MFA.
    Policies that only act on Identity Protection risk do not count.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdMfaAllUsers

    Returns true when a policy requires MFA for all users on all cloud apps.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1504
    #>
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'All users is the name of the Conditional Access scope.')]
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1504',
        Title = 'Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users of the organisation''s online services.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1504', 'essential-eight:ISM-0974', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(2)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policies = @(Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy -Scope AllUsers)
    $testResult = $policies.Count -gt 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. These Conditional Access policies require multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps:`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps.'
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjects $policies -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    return $testResult
}

=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1649.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that privileged directory roles have no permanent active assignments, so that administration is just-in-time.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1649 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Three) asks that just-in-time
    administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.

    The check reads the active assignments of every directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged.
    An assignment that has no end date and was not made through an activation is permanent, and fails the
    check; eligible assignments and time-bound active assignments made with Privileged Identity Management
    pass. The emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are
    left out, because a break glass account is meant to hold its role permanently.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration

    Returns true when no privileged role has a permanent active assignment outside the emergency access accounts.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1649
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1649',
        Title = 'Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'privileged-identity-management',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'DirectoryRole',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1098.003', 'T1078.004'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1649', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(7)', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(5)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2', 'Entra_Identity_Governance'),
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $roles = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' -Select id, displayName, isPrivileged | Where-Object { $_.isPrivileged -eq $true })
    $roleName = @{}
    foreach ($role in $roles) { $roleName[$role.id] = $role.displayName }

    # Eligible assignments are read too: EligibleChecked tells whether the PIM APIs answered, which is what makes an assignment just-in-time.
    $read = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal
    if (-not $read.EligibleChecked) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Privileged Identity Management is not available in this tenant, so every assignment is permanent. Just-in-time administration needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance.'
        return $null
    }
    $breakGlass = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount | ForEach-Object ObjectId)

    $permanent = @($read.Assignments | Where-Object {
            $_.AssignmentType -eq 'Active' -and
            $roleName.ContainsKey($_.roleDefinitionId) -and
            [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($_.endDateTime) -and
            $_.principalId -notin $breakGlass
        })
    $testResult = $permanent.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. No privileged directory role has a permanent active assignment. $($roles.Count) privileged roles were checked$(if ($breakGlass.Count -gt 0) { ", leaving out $($breakGlass.Count) emergency access account(s)" })."
    } else {
        $table = "| Role | Principal | Type | Scope |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($assignment in ($permanent | Sort-Object { $roleName[$_.roleDefinitionId] }, { $_.principal.displayName })) {
            $principal = $assignment.principal
            $name = if ($principal.userPrincipalName) { $principal.userPrincipalName } elseif ($principal.displayName) { $principal.displayName } else { $assignment.principalId }
            $type = ([string]$principal.'@odata.type') -replace '^#microsoft\.graph\.', ''
            $table += "| $($roleName[$assignment.roleDefinitionId]) | $name | $type | $($assignment.directoryScopeId) |`n"
        }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($permanent.Count) permanent active assignment(s) to privileged directory roles were found. Make them eligible in Privileged Identity Management so that administrators activate the role when they need it.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1403.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that the Microsoft Entra smart lockout threshold is five failed sign-ins or fewer.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1403 (Guidelines for system access, User account lockouts) asks that user accounts, except for break
    glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed
    logon attempts. This control is not part of the Essential Eight Maturity Model.

    Microsoft Entra smart lockout locks an account for the lockout duration after the configured number of
    failed sign-ins, and tracks familiar and unfamiliar locations separately. The check reads the tenant's
    Password Rule Settings and passes when the lockout threshold is explicitly set to the maximum given
    (5 by default) or fewer. The Microsoft default of 10 fails.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold

    Returns true when the smart lockout threshold is 5 or fewer.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1403
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1403',
        Title = 'User accounts are protected by lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'password-protection',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1110',
        Control = ('ism:ISM-1403', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The most failed sign-ins allowed before an account is locked.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumFailedAttempts = 5
    )

    $settings = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'settings' -ApiVersion beta
    $rawValue = $settings.values | Where-Object name -EQ 'LockoutThreshold' | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty value
    $isSet = -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$rawValue)
    $threshold = if ($isSet) { [int]$rawValue } else { 10 }
    $testResult = $isSet -and $threshold -le $MaximumFailedAttempts

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins, which is $MaximumFailedAttempts or fewer."
    } elseif (-not $isSet) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is not set explicitly, so the Microsoft default of **10** failed sign-ins applies. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1648.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that no enabled account with a privileged directory role has been inactive for 45 days or more.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1648 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Two) asks that privileged
    access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

    The check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra
    marks as privileged, and reads the last sign-in of each. A user fails when the account is enabled and the
    most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is older than the number of days given (45 by
    default), or when the account has never signed in and was created before that. The emergency access
    accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are
    meant to stay unused.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess

    Returns true when every enabled privileged user signed in within the last 45 days.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1648
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1648',
        Title = 'Privileged access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'roles',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1648', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(3)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Days without a sign-in after which privileged access must be disabled.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $InactiveDays = 45
    )

    $rolesOf = Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser
    if ($rolesOf.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }

    $cutoff = [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId @($rolesOf.Keys) -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, accountEnabled, createdDateTime, signInActivity)
    $inactive = foreach ($user in $users) {
        if ($user.accountEnabled -ne $true) { continue }
        $signIns = @($user.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime, $user.signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { [datetime]$_ })
        $lastSignIn = if ($signIns.Count -gt 0) { ($signIns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum.ToUniversalTime() } else { $null }
        $isInactive = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff } else { $user.createdDateTime -and ([datetime]$user.createdDateTime).ToUniversalTime() -lt $cutoff }
        if ($isInactive) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                id                = $user.id
                displayName       = $user.displayName
                userPrincipalName = $user.userPrincipalName
                LastSignIn        = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { 'Never' }
                Roles             = $rolesOf[$user.id] -join ', '
            }
        }
    }
    $inactive = @($inactive)
    $testResult = $inactive.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Every enabled user with a privileged directory role signed in within the last $InactiveDays days ($($rolesOf.Count) users checked)."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Last sign-in | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in ($inactive | Sort-Object userPrincipalName)) { $table += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.LastSignIn) | $($user.Roles) |`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($inactive.Count) enabled user(s) with a privileged directory role have not signed in for $InactiveDays days or more. Disable the account or remove the role, and let an access review or a PIM alert catch the next one.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtAsdDedicatedPrivilegedAccount {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that users with a privileged directory role have no Exchange Online mailbox, so that the account is dedicated to privileged duties.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-0445 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level One) asks that privileged
    users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged
    access, and ISM-1175 that privileged user accounts are prevented from accessing the internet, email and
    web services.

    A mailbox on an administrator account is the usual sign that the account is also used for everyday work,
    and it exposes the privileged account to phishing. The check lists the users with an active or eligible
    assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged, and fails for each one that has an
    enabled Exchange Online service plan that provides a mailbox (Plan 1, Plan 2, Kiosk or Essentials). The
    Exchange Foundation plan that comes with Entra ID, Intune and Defender licences creates no mailbox and is
    not counted. The emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration
    (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdDedicatedPrivilegedAccount

    Returns true when no privileged user has an Exchange Online mailbox.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-0445
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-0445',
        Title = 'Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'roles',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1566'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-0445', 'essential-eight:ISM-1175', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(2)', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(5)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The IDs of the Exchange Online service plans that provide a mailbox: Plan 2, Plan 1, Kiosk and Essentials.
        [string[]] $MailboxServicePlanId = @(
            'efb87545-963c-4e0d-99df-69c6916d9eb0',
            '9aaf7827-d63c-4b61-89c3-182f06f82e5c',
            '4a82b400-a79f-41a4-b4e2-e94f5787b113',
            '1126bef5-da20-4f07-b45e-ad25d2581aa8'
        )
    )

    $rolesOf = Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser
    if ($rolesOf.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }

    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId @($rolesOf.Keys) -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, assignedPlans)
    $withMailbox = @($users | Where-Object {
            @($_.assignedPlans | Where-Object { $_.servicePlanId -in $MailboxServicePlanId -and $_.capabilityStatus -eq 'Enabled' }).Count -gt 0
        } | ForEach-Object {
            [pscustomobject]@{ id = $_.id; displayName = $_.displayName; userPrincipalName = $_.userPrincipalName; Roles = $rolesOf[$_.id] -join ', ' }
        })
    $testResult = $withMailbox.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. None of the $($rolesOf.Count) users with a privileged directory role has an Exchange Online mailbox."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in ($withMailbox | Sort-Object userPrincipalName)) { $table += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.Roles) |`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($withMailbox.Count) of $($rolesOf.Count) users with a privileged directory role have an Exchange Online mailbox. Give each administrator a separate, unlicensed account for privileged duties and move the role to it.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

input.prompt:
Research task (read-only, no code changes). I'm reviewing a Maester PR that adds Microsoft 365 checks for Australia's ASD Essential Eight and ISM controls. I need the authoritative ASD wording for each control so I can tell whether ASD specifies implementation details (e.g. which roles count as privileged, whether a specific authentication strength is required, what counts as "permanent", a numeric threshold, which apps/rules) or stays at the level of a generic outcome.

Controls: ISM-1504, ISM-0974, ISM-1173, ISM-1872, ISM-1649, ISM-1648, ISM-0445, ISM-1175, ISM-1403, ISM-1488, ISM-1672, ISM-1673, ISM-1654, ISM-1667, ISM-1668, ISM-1669, ISM-1695.

Sources, in order of authority:
1. The ISM itself on cyber.gov.au (current release; it's published as "Guidelines for ..." chapters, and also as OSCAL/XML/Excel downloads at https://www.cyber.gov.au/resources-business-and-government/essential-cyber-security/ism and the GitHub repo AustralianCyberSecurityCentre/ism-oscal). The OSCAL JSON on GitHub is the easiest way to get exact control text.
2. The Essential Eight Maturity Model (cyber.gov.au) and the "Essential Eight maturity model and ISM mapping" publication, including which maturity level each control sits at.
3. "Essential Eight assessment process guide" (cyber.gov.au), which tells assessors what evidence to look for and what test methods to use for each control. This is the key source for implementation specifics, e.g. how "privileged" is defined, what "phishing-resistant" means, how lockout is tested.
4. The ISM's own definitions/glossary for terms like "privileged user", "phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication", "just-in-time administration", "online services".

Third-party sites (myctrl.tools, ismcontrol.pages.dev, Microsoft Learn) are fine for finding things but quote ASD's own documents for the answer, and say when you could only find a third-party copy.

For each control return:
- the exact control text (verbatim) and the ISM release/date you read it from;
- its Essential Eight strategy and maturity level (or "not in Essential Eight");
- any ASD-specified detail that goes beyond the control text: definitions, assessment-guide test methods, thresholds, lists. Quote it verbatim with the URL/document and section;
- one line: "Specific" or "Generic", meaning whether ASD tells you how to implement/measure it in a way that would decide between two implementations (examples of what the two implementations disagree on: whether only permanent active role assignments fail vs any active assignment; whether a CA policy must target "all users" or just a set of admin roles and which roles; whether phishing resistance is judged by the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" authentication strength or by allowed methods; lockout threshold 5 vs 10; whether "privileged" means Entra's isPrivileged roles or a fixed list).

Also report specifically:
- How ASD defines "privileged user" / "privileged access" (does it list roles?).
- What ASD considers phishing-resistant MFA (which methods).
- Whether ISM-1649 "just-in-time" is defined, and whether time-bound active assignments are acceptable.
- Whether ISM-1403's "five failed logon attempts" applies to cloud identity smart lockout and whether risk-based lockout counts.
- For ISM-1667/1668/1669/1488/1672/1673/1654/1695: the exact text and any specific settings ASD names (e.g. ASR rule names, macro settings).

Keep the report factual and compact, with URLs for every quote. Don't speculate about Maester code.

Research task (read-only, no code changes). I'm reviewing a Maester PR that adds Microsoft 365 checks for Australia's ASD Essential Eight and ISM controls. I need to know exactly what the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud (https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/) and ASD's Microsoft hardening guides prescribe, so I can tell whether ASD specifies settings that differ from CIS Microsoft 365 / CISA SCuBA, or leaves them generic.

Site map (found already): /configuration/entra-id/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/, /design/platform/identity/conditional-access/, /design/platform/identity/tenant/, /configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/, /configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/ (including asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled and asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers), /design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/, /design/platform/client/device-updates/, /security-and-governance/ (Essential Eight pages). Also look for privileged access / PIM / roles pages anywhere under /configuration/entra-id/ or /design/platform/identity/ (try identity governance, roles and administrators, privileged identity management). The blueprint is also on GitHub (search for the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud repository) which may be easier to read.

Also check ASD's hardening publications on cyber.gov.au: "Hardening Microsoft Windows 10 and Windows 11 workstations", "Microsoft Office macro security", "Restricting Microsoft Office macros", "Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, Office 2019 and Office 2016".

For each topic, quote the specific settings verbatim (with URL) and say what they are:
1. Conditional Access: the list of policies the blueprint defines (names and what each targets/grants). Specifically: is there an "MFA for all users" policy, what users/apps it targets and exclusions; is there a separate admin policy and which roles it targets (list them); does it use the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" authentication strength or a custom one, and for whom (all users or admins).
2. Authentication strengths: which methods the blueprint allows.
3. Privileged access: does the blueprint require PIM, eligible-only assignments, time-bound active assignments, activation duration, approval; separate admin accounts without mailboxes/licences; cloud-only admin accounts; inactivity disabling (45 days?) or access reviews.
4. Smart lockout / password protection: the lockout threshold and duration values it sets.
5. Intune ASR: which ASR rules it sets and in what mode (block/audit/warn); specifically rules for Office apps creating child processes, Office creating executable content, Office injecting into other processes, Win32 API calls from Office macros, and any others.
6. Office macros: the settings for "block macros from the internet", "VBA macros notification", macro antivirus scanning, trusted publishers, Win32 API.
7. Internet Explorer 11: disabled or removed, and how (setting name).
8. Windows Update rings / patching: deadlines/days (quality, feature), grace periods, which Intune setting.

Return a compact report organised by those 8 topics, verbatim quotes with URLs, and a final list of every place where the blueprint names a concrete value (a number, a role list, an authentication strength, a rule mode). Say clearly when the blueprint is silent on something. Don't speculate about Maester code.

﻿function Test-MtIntuneASRRules {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Ensure the Microsoft Defender ASR Standard Protection baseline rules are configured in Block or Audit mode.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks Intune Windows configuration policies (configurationPolicies API) for ASR rule
    configurations. Covers both Endpoint Security Attack Surface Reduction profiles and Settings
    catalog policies, since ASR rules share the same setting definition IDs in both.

    ASR rules reduce the attack surface of applications by preventing behaviors commonly abused by malware,
    such as Office macros spawning child processes, credential theft from LSASS, or execution of obfuscated scripts.

    Each ASR rule can be set to one of four modes:
    - Block: Actively prevents the behavior (recommended for production)
    - Audit: Logs the event without blocking (recommended for testing)
    - Warn: Warns the user before allowing the behavior
    - Disabled/Not configured: Rule is inactive

    Pass criteria:
    The test passes if every rule in the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint ASR Standard Protection baseline is
    configured in Block or Audit mode in at least one ASR policy. The Standard Protection baseline is the
    minimum recommended set Microsoft publishes for initial ASR deployment:

    1. Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
    2. Block credential stealing from LSASS
    3. Block persistence through WMI event subscription

    See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-deployment-implement

    Additional ASR rules detected in tenant policies are reported for visibility but do not affect the pass/fail result.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtIntuneASRRules

    Returns true if every Standard Protection baseline rule is configured in Block or Audit mode across the union of all ASR policies in the tenant.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtIntuneASRRules
    #>
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'ASR Rules is the official Microsoft product name')]
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'MT.1178',
        Title = 'Ensure ASR Rules are configured correctly.',
        Product = 'intune',
        RelatedProduct = 'defender',
        Feature = 'endpoint-security',
        Area = 'devices',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1003.001', 'T1546.003', 'T1068'),
        Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:CM-7', 'nist-800-53-r5:SI-3'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'INTUNE_A',
        Author = 'OfirGavish',
        Contributor = 'royklo'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    try {
        Write-Verbose "Querying Intune Windows configuration policies..."
        $candidatePolicies = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "deviceManagement/configurationPolicies?`$filter=platforms has 'windows10'&`$select=id,name,description,templateReference" -ApiVersion beta)

        Write-Verbose "Found $($candidatePolicies.Count) Windows configuration policies to inspect."

        # Friendly names for ASR rules (extracted from setting definition IDs)
        $asrRuleNames = @{
            'blockexecutionofpotentiallyobfuscatedscripts'                                           = 'Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts'
            'blockwin32apicallsfromofficemacros'                                                     = 'Block Win32 API calls from Office macros'
            'blockexecutablefilesrunningunlesstheymeetprevalenceagetrustedlistcriterion'              = 'Block executable files unless they meet prevalence/age/trusted list criteria'
            'blockofficecommunicationappfromcreatingchildprocesses'                                   = 'Block Office communication app from creating child processes'
            'blockallofficeapplicationsfromcreatingchildprocesses'                                    = 'Block all Office applications from creating child processes'
            'blockadobereaderfromcreatingchildprocesses'                                              = 'Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes'
            'blockcredentialstealingfromwindowslocalsecurityauthoritysubsystem'                       = 'Block credential stealing from LSASS'
            'blockjavascriptorvbscriptfromlaunchingdownloadedexecutablecontent'                       = 'Block JavaScript/VBScript from launching downloaded executable content'
            'blockuntrustedunsignedprocessesthatrunfromusb'                                           = 'Block untrusted/unsigned processes from USB'
            'blockpersistencethroughwmieventsubscription'                                             = 'Block persistence through WMI event subscription'
            'blockuseofcopiedorimpersonatedsystemtools'                                               = 'Block use of copied or impersonated system tools'
            'blockabuseofexploitedvulnerablesigneddrivers'                                            = 'Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers'
            'blockprocesscreationsfrompsexecandwmicommands'                                           = 'Block process creations from PSExec and WMI commands'
            'blockofficeapplicationsfromcreatingexecutablecontent'                                    = 'Block Office applications from creating executable content'
            'blockofficeapplicationsfrominjectingcodeintootherprocesses'                              = 'Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes'
            'blockrebootingmachineinsafemode'                                                         = 'Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode'
            'useadvancedprotectionagainstransomware'                                                  = 'Use advanced protection against ransomware'
            'blockexecutablecontentfromemailclientandwebmail'                                         = 'Block executable content from email client and webmail'
            'blockwebshellcreationforservers'                                                         = 'Block webshell creation for servers'
        }

        # Microsoft Standard Protection baseline (minimum recommended ASR rules per Defender deployment guide).
        # Pass requires every rule in this set to be Block or Audit across the union of all ASR policies.
        $standardProtectionRuleSuffixes = @{
            'blockabuseofexploitedvulnerablesigneddrivers'                                            = 'Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers'
            'blockcredentialstealingfromwindowslocalsecurityauthoritysubsystem'                       = 'Block credential stealing from LSASS'
            'blockpersistencethroughwmieventsubscription'                                             = 'Block persistence through WMI event subscription'
        }

        $policyResults = [System.Collections.Generic.List[hashtable]]::new()
        # Track best mode seen across the union of all policies for each baseline rule.
        # Priority: Block > Audit > Warn > Disabled > Not configured.
        $baselineRuleStatus = @{}
        foreach ($k in $standardProtectionRuleSuffixes.Keys) { $baselineRuleStatus[$k] = 'Not configured' }

        $modeRank = @{ 'Block' = 4; 'Audit' = 3; 'Warn' = 2; 'Disabled' = 1; 'Not configured' = 0 }

        foreach ($policy in $candidatePolicies) {
            Write-Verbose "Checking policy: $($policy.name) ($($policy.id))"
            $settingsUri = "deviceManagement/configurationPolicies('$($policy.id)')/settings?`$expand=settingDefinitions&`$top=1000"
            $settingsResponse = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri $settingsUri -ApiVersion beta)

            $blockCount = 0
            $auditCount = 0
            $warnCount = 0
            $disabledCount = 0
            $notConfiguredCount = 0
            $ruleDetails = [System.Collections.Generic.List[hashtable]]::new()

            foreach ($setting in $settingsResponse) {
                $defId = $setting.settingInstance.settingDefinitionId
                if ($defId -ne 'device_vendor_msft_policy_config_defender_attacksurfacereductionrules') { continue }

                # ASR rules are stored in a groupSettingCollectionValue
                foreach ($group in $setting.settingInstance.groupSettingCollectionValue) {
                    foreach ($child in $group.children) {
                        $childDefId = $child.settingDefinitionId
                        $val = $child.choiceSettingValue.value

                        # Extract rule name from definition ID
                        $ruleSuffix = $childDefId -replace '^device_vendor_msft_policy_config_defender_attacksurfacereductionrules_', ''
                        $friendlyName = if ($asrRuleNames.ContainsKey($ruleSuffix)) { $asrRuleNames[$ruleSuffix] } else { $ruleSuffix }

                        # Determine enforcement mode from value suffix
                        $mode = 'Not configured'
                        if ($val -like '*_block') { $mode = 'Block'; $blockCount++ }
                        elseif ($val -like '*_audit') { $mode = 'Audit'; $auditCount++ }
                        elseif ($val -like '*_warn') { $mode = 'Warn'; $warnCount++ }
                        elseif ($val -like '*_off') { $mode = 'Disabled'; $disabledCount++ }
                        else { $notConfiguredCount++ }

Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Learn ## Overview Privileged Identity Management (PIM) generates alerts when there's suspicious or unsafe activity in your organization in Microsoft Entra ID. When an alert is triggered, it shows up on the Privileged Identity Management dashboard. Select the alert to see a report that lists the users or roles that triggered the alert. Note One event in Privileged Identity Management can generate email notifications to multiple recipients – assignees, approvers, or administrators. The maximum number of notifications sent per one event is 1000. If the number of recipients exceeds 1000 – only the first 1000 recipients will receive an email notification. This doesn't prevent other assignees, administrators, or approvers from using their permissions in Microsoft Entra ID and Privileged Identity Management. ![Screenshot that shows the alerts page with a list of alerts and their severity.](media/pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts/view-alerts.png) ## License requirements Using Privileged Identity Management requires licenses. For more information on licensing, see [Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing fundamentals](../licensing-fundamentals) . ## Security alerts This section lists all the security alerts for Microsoft Entra roles, along with how to fix them and how to prevent them. Severity has the following meaning: - **High**: Requires immediate action because of a policy violation. - **Medium**: Doesn't require immediate action but signals a potential policy violation. - **Low**: Doesn't require immediate action but suggests a preferable policy change. Note Only the following roles are able to read PIM security alerts for Microsoft Entra roles: **Global Administrator**, **Privileged Role Administrator**, **Global Reader**, **Security Administrator**, and **Security Reader**. ### Administrators aren't using their privileged roles Severity: **Low** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | Users that have assigned privileged roles they don't need increase the chances of an attack. It's also easier for attackers to remain unnoticed in accounts that aren't actively being used. | | **How to fix?** | Review the users in the list and remove them from privileged roles that they don't need. | | **Prevention** | Assign privileged roles only to users who have a business justification. Schedule regular [access reviews](pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review) to verify that users still need their access. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | Removes the account from their privileged role. | | **Trigger** | Triggered if a user goes over a specified number of days without activating a role. | | **Number of days** | This setting specifies the maximum number of days, from 0 to 100, that a user can go without activating a role. | ### Roles don't require multifactor authentication for activation Severity: **Low** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | Without multifactor authentication, compromised users can activate privileged roles. | | **How to fix?** | Review the list of roles and [require multifactor authentication](pim-how-to-change-default-settings) for every role. | | **Prevention** | [Require MFA](pim-how-to-change-default-settings) for every role. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | Makes multifactor authentication required for activation of the privileged role. | ### The organization doesn't have Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance Severity: **Low** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | The current Microsoft Entra organization doesn't have Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance. | | **How to fix?** | Review information about [Microsoft Entra editions](../../fundamentals/licensing). Upgrade to Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance. | ### Potential stale accounts in a privileged role Severity: **Medium** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | This alert is no longer triggered based on the last password change date of for an account. This alert is for accounts in a privileged role that haven't signed in during the past *n* days, where *n* is a configurable number of days between 1 and 365. These accounts might be service or shared accounts that aren't being maintained and are vulnerable to attackers. | | **How to fix?** | Review the accounts in the list. If they no longer need access, remove them from their privileged roles. | | **Prevention** | Ensure that accounts that are shared are rotating strong passwords when there's a change in the users that know the password. Regularly review accounts with privileged roles using [access reviews](pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review) and remove role assignments that are no longer needed. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | Removes the account from their privileged role. | | **Best practices** | Shared, service, and emergency access accounts that authenticate using a password and are assigned to highly privileged administrative roles such as Global Administrator or Security Administrator should have their passwords rotated for the following cases:
- After a security incident involving misuse or compromise of administrative access rights
- After any user's privileges are changed so that they're no longer an administrator (for example, after an employee who was an administrator leaves IT or leaves the organization)
- At regular intervals (for example, quarterly or yearly), even if there was no known breach or change to IT staffing

Since multiple people have access to these accounts' credentials, the credentials should be rotated to ensure that people that have left their roles can no longer access the accounts. [Learn more about securing accounts](../../identity/role-based-access-control/security-planning) | ### Roles are being assigned outside of Privileged Identity Management Severity: **High** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | Privileged role assignments made outside of Privileged Identity Management aren't properly monitored and might indicate an active attack. | | **How to fix?** | Review the users in the list and remove them from privileged roles assigned outside of Privileged Identity Management. You can also enable or disable both the alert and its accompanying email notification in the alert settings. | | **Prevention** | Investigate where users are being assigned privileged roles outside of Privileged Identity Management and prohibit future assignments from there. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | Removes the user from their privileged role. | Note PIM sends email notifications for the **Role assigned outside of PIM** alert when the alert is enabled from alert settings. For Microsoft Entra roles in PIM, emails are sent to **Privileged Role Administrators**, **Security Administrators**, and **Global Administrators** that have enabled Privileged Identity Management. For Azure resources in PIM, emails are sent to **Owners** and **User Access Administrators**. ### There are too many Global Administrators Severity: **Low** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | Global Administrator is the highest privileged role. If a Global Administrator is compromised, the attacker gains access to all of their permissions, which put your whole system at risk. | | **How to fix?** | Review the users in the list and remove any that don't absolutely need the Global Administrator role. Assign lower privileged roles to these users instead. | | **Prevention** | Assign users the least privileged role they need. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | Removes the account from their privileged role. | | **Trigger** | Triggered if two different criteria are met, and you can configure both of them. First, you need to reach a certain threshold of Global Administrator role assignments. Second, a certain percentage of your total role assignments must be Global Administrators. If you only meet one of these measurements, the alert doesn't appear. | | **Minimum number of Global Administrators** | This setting specifies the number of Global Administrator role assignments, from 2 to 100, that you consider to be too few for your Microsoft Entra organization. | | **Percentage of Global Administrators** | This setting specifies the minimum percentage of administrators who are Global Administrators, from 0% to 100%, below which you don't want your Microsoft Entra organization to dip. | ### Roles are being activated too frequently Severity: **Low** | - | Description | | --- | --- | | **Why do I get this alert?** | Multiple activations to the same privileged role by the same user is a sign of an attack. | | **How to fix?** | Review the users in the list and ensure that the [activation duration](pim-how-to-change-default-settings) for their privileged role is set long enough for them to perform their tasks. | | **Prevention** | Ensure that the [activation duration](pim-how-to-change-default-settings) for privileged roles is set long enough for users to perform their tasks.[Require multifactor authentication](pim-how-to-change-default-settings) for privileged roles that have accounts shared by multiple administrators. | | **In-portal mitigation action** | N/A | | **Trigger** | Triggered if a user activates the same privileged role multiple times within a specified period. You can configure both the time period and the number of activations. | | **Activation renewal timeframe** | This setting specifies in days, hours, minutes, and seconds the time period you want to use to track suspicious renewals. | | **Number of activation renewals** | This setting specifies the number of activations, from 2 to 100, at which you would like to be notified, within the timeframe you chose. You can change this setting by moving the slider, or typing a number in the text box. | ## Customize security alert settings Follow these steps to configure security alerts for Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management: 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Privileged Role Administrator](../../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#privileged-role-administrator). 2. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Alerts** > **Setting**. For information about how to add the Privileged Identity Management tile to your dashboard, see [Start using Privileged Identity Management](pim-getting-started). ![Screenshot of the alerts page with the settings highlighted.](media/pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts/alert-settings.png) 3. Customize settings on the different alerts to work with your environment and security goals. ![Screenshot of the alert setting page.](media/pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts/security-alert-settings.png)

result.output:
Maester looks up each `Control` value of a test, in the order they are written. A value resolves when its key is
a framework that has a file and its ID is a requirement in that file.

- `Benchmark` is built from the first value that resolves: the `Framework`, its `Version`, the `Requirement` and
  the requirement's own facts. When no value resolves, `Benchmark` is `null`.
- `Control` holds the values the test wrote, followed by the `Related` references of every requirement that
  resolved, each once.

`Get-MtTest` shows both. See [the result schema](../result-schema.md#benchmark).

A framework is found by its key, whatever suite declares it. A custom test can name a framework that ships with
Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`) or one that a suite in your own test folder declares. Two suites
must not declare the same key: Maester warns, names both `suite.json` files and uses the first, and a framework
that ships with Maester comes before one of yours.

A `Control` value whose key no framework file has, such as `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)` or `iso-27001-2022:A.5.17`,
is written to the result as it is. It needs no file.

A problem with a framework never stops a run. Maester writes a warning that names the file and what is wrong:

- The file is missing or is not valid JSON, its `Framework` or `Version` differs from the `suite.json`, a
  requirement has no `Id` or an `Id` that is listed twice, or a `Related` reference is not written
  `<framework-key>:<control-id>`. No test gets a `Benchmark` or `Related` controls from that framework.
- A `Control` names a framework that has a file and a requirement that is not in it, usually a typing error. That
  value gives no `Benchmark`; the other tests keep theirs.

#### Mapping a test to a framework

| The test | What to write | What the result gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implements a requirement of a benchmark that has a framework file (`CIS.M365.5.1.5.1`, `CONTOSO.BL.1.1`) | `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`. If the requirement is new, add it to the framework file. | `Benchmark`, and the reference in `Control` |
| Exists for its own reasons and also supports such a requirement (a Maester test that checks what a CISA policy asks for) | `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` | The same |
| Supports a control of a framework that has no file | `Control = 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)'` | The reference in `Control` |

A test can list several values. Put the requirement the test is written for first: the first value that resolves
becomes the `Benchmark`. Use the keys and requirement IDs of the framework files that ship with Maester so your
results line up with the built-in ones. For a framework that has no file, choose a lowercase key such as
`nist-800-53-r5` or `iso-27001-2022` and keep to it.

#### Why the framework file still exists

A `key:id` string names a requirement. It cannot hold what is true of the requirement whatever test implements
it. The framework file holds that:

- the name and the version of the framework, in one place, so a new version of a benchmark is one edit;

nothing runs.
- Unknown IDs are listed in the result under `Selection.UnknownIds`. An ID under a declared family's parent ID is
  never unknown, so you can keep a row for an instance that does not exist in this run.

### Tags

A tag selects a test that carries it in the `Tag` of its `[MaesterTest]` attribute, or whose folder's
`suite.json` lists it under `Tags`. Tags are for your own tests. The tests that ship with Maester no longer
carry tags for their suite, product, topic or severity, because each of those is an attribute.

The tags of Maester 2.x keep working. `-Tag CA`, `-Tag CIS`, `-ExcludeTag MS.AAD.3.5` and every other 2.x tag
select the built-in tests that carried the tag in 2.x, and the ID of a built-in test is still one of its tags,
so `-Tag MT.1068` selects it. A run that selects through a 2.x tag writes one warning that names the tag and,
where there is one, the selector that replaces it. Tests added after Maester 3.0 do not carry 2.x tags, so move
to the selectors when you can:

| 2.x tag | Example | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Suite | `CISA`, `Maester` | `-Suite cisa` |
| Product or service | `EXO`, `Entra` | `-Product exchange` |
| Topic | `CA`, `Privileged` | `-Feature conditional-access`, `-Area privileged-access` |
| Benchmark control ID | `MS.AAD.3.5` | `-TestId CISA.MS.AAD.3.5` |
| Severity | `Severity:High` | `-Severity High` |
| A test's ID | `MT.1068` | `-TestId MT.1068` |

The 2.x tags and the test ID are used for selection only. A result row's `Tag` lists the tags written in the
test, and its `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `Suite` and `Severity` fields say the rest.

Deselected and disabled tests still appear in the result as `NotRun` rows with a reason code. See
[Applicability and reason codes](./applicability.md).

## TestSettings

One row per test you want to change, built-in or custom, native or Pester-format.

| Key | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | string | The test ID, or a family instance ID (`MT.1024.<suffix>`). Required. |
| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low` or `Info`. Overrides the test's own severity. |
| `Enabled` | bool | `false` turns the test off: it is not run and appears as `NotRun` with reason `DisabledByConfig`. `true` admits it in `DefaultAction: Skip` mode. |
| `Reason` | string | Shown as the reason of a disabled test. |

result.output:
**(1) MS.AAD.7.4v1 (permanent active role assignments)**

- Policy: "Permanent active role assignments SHALL NOT be allowed for highly privileged roles."
- Rationale: "Instead of giving users permanent assignments to privileged roles, provisioning access when the roles are needed"
- Exceptions listed in the notes:
  - "Emergency access accounts that need perpetual access to the tenant"
  - "Some types of service accounts that require a user account with privileged roles"
- The Implementation section adds one more exception: "If using PIM for Groups, a group that is enrolled in PIM is allowed to have a perpetual active assignment"

**(2) MS.AAD.3.1v1 and MS.AAD.3.6v1**

- MS.AAD.3.1v1 policy: "Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users."
- MS.AAD.3.1v1 notes: "The phishing-resistant methods of Microsoft Entra ID certificate-based authentication (CBA), FIDO2 Security Key," and "Windows Hello for Business, and device-bound passkeys" (the note adds "in the authenticator application of choice")
- The document says these methods "offer forms of MFA with the fewest weaknesses." The notes also say that, for federal agencies, "Microsoft Entra ID CBA supports federal PIV card authentication directly to Microsoft Entra ID."
- MS.AAD.3.6v1 policy: "Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be required for highly privileged roles."
- MS.AAD.3.6v1 note: "Refer to the "Highly Privileged Roles" section at the top of this baseline"

Per the document, SCuBA counts CBA, FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business, and device-bound passkeys as phishing-resistant. The document does not give a separate definitive list beyond these.

**(3) Highly privileged roles (as defined by SCuBA)**

- Global Administrator
- Privileged Role Administrator
- User Administrator
- SharePoint Administrator
- Exchange Administrator
- Hybrid Identity Administrator
- Application Administrator
- Cloud Application Administrator

**(4) MS.AAD.3.2v2 (MFA for all users)**

- Policy: "MFA SHALL be enforced for all users."
- Rationale: "This policy helps protect the tenant for guest users or any other group with multifactor authentication"

The rationale continues with "where phishing-resistant MFA is not enforceable due to technical limitations," which I've omitted here to stay within the 125-character limit per quote.
