## When to Use This Skill

- Creating a new Maester security check
- Editing or refactoring an existing check
- Adding or correcting a check's attributes: product, feature, area, resource type, severity, user impact,
  implementation cost, ATT&CK techniques, service or licence declarations
- Writing or updating a check's `.md` (description, remediation, result template)
- Reviewing a check for correctness, attributes that fit the rubric, or documentation completeness
- Debugging a failing, erroring or skipped check
- Writing or converting a user's custom test (`custom/` folder)

**Do NOT use this skill for:**

- Editing EIDSCA tests by hand -- `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` are generated by `build/eidsca/Update-EidscaTests.ps1`
  from templates in `build/eidsca/templates/`. Change the generator or its data.
- Editing ORCA tests by hand -- `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` (header "Generated by ./build/orca/Update-OrcaTests.ps1")
  and `powershell/internal/generated/orca/check-ORCA*.ps1` are generated. Change the generator.
- Editing `website/docs/tests/` -- test pages are generated from the test files by
  `website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs`.
- Unit tests of the module itself (`powershell/tests/`).

## Prerequisites
### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
- [ ] `Id`, `Title`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `Author` set;
      values constant.
- [ ] `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` set, or both left out when `Severity` is `Info`.
- [ ] `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`; a
      new key is added there in this pull request.
- [ ] Each of those values, and `RelatedProduct` if set, checked against its section of the
      [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), with the reason visible in
      the description or the remediation text.
- [ ] No `Category` or `Preview`; no `Tag` for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence,
      severity or the ID. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag where they apply.
- [ ] A CIS, CISA or ASD check sets `Control` to its requirement (`cis-m365:<id>`, `cis-github:<id>`, `essential-eight:<id>` or
      `cisa-scuba:<id>`), first, and the requirement is in the suite's framework file.
- [ ] `Control` was considered for every check: a CIS or CISA requirement that asks for the same setting, and
      NIST SP 800-53 controls from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json` (none when a `cisa-scuba`
      reference already brings them). Left empty only when nothing applies.
- [ ] `[CmdletBinding()]` and `[OutputType([bool])]`; comment-based help inside the function.
- [ ] `Get-MtTest <ID>` (without `-Path`) reports no errors.

### Documentation
- [ ] `.md` has summary, rationale, `#### Remediation action` with portal links, and ends with `<!--- Results --->` + `%TestResult%`.
- [ ] No scaffold placeholder is left in the `.md` ("Describe what this test checks", "Explain how to fix"), and its links open the page they name.
- [ ] Pass message starts with "Well done."; fail message is actionable.

### Code style
- [ ] One True Brace Style; Pascal Case; full cmdlet names (no aliases); 4-space indentation.
- [ ] UTF-8 with BOM for `.ps1` files.

### Pre-pull request
- [ ] `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` passes (PSScriptAnalyzer included).
- [ ] Ran against a tenant with `Invoke-MtTest`.
- [ ] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).

## Common Mistakes

---
name: map-benchmarks-to-existing-tests
description: Benchmark tests that duplicate another suite's check must be shims; review every new test for duplicates against the benchmark's own sources
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a benchmark suite (CIS, CISA, ASD, ...) needs a check that another suite's test already does, the new test is a **shim**: own Id, Title, Control, guide; body is `return <other test's function>` (with a parameter when the benchmark names a different value, e.g. ASD lockout 5 vs CIS 10). A check of its own only when the benchmark's own sources (audit/assessment guidance, reference configuration such as ASD Blueprint) ask for something different. Generic helpers never carry a suite name (`Get-MtAsd*`); they go in `internal/services/<service>/`. Decided 2026-10-29 on PR 2552; written into AGENTS.md ("Reviewing a test for duplicates"), the writing-tests guide ("Tests that another suite already has"), the maester-test-expert skill/agents, and enforced by `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`.

**Why:** the owner caught that my first review of PR 2552 would have accepted the ASD tests as written, duplicating CIS/CISA logic. Shims keep one implementation while each benchmark keeps its own row (with its Benchmark facts such as E8 maturity level). Mapping a Control onto another suite's test alone loses that, and Maester has no framework selector.

**How to apply:** in every test review or authoring task, search all suites for the same setting first, read the benchmark's primary sources, and fail a review that re-implements an existing check without a reason from those sources. Related: [[maester-3-design]].

input.content:
Thanks @jusso-dev. The framework files and the suite plumbing are well done. I've pushed a refactor to your branch. The main change: where ASD asks for what another suite already checks, the ASD test now runs that suite's test instead of carrying its own copy.

**What ASD's sources say.** I checked each control against the ISM (September 2026), the [Essential Eight assessment process guide](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-assessment-process-guide) and the [ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/). The ISM text is generic, and where ASD does get specific, it matches an existing test:

- **ISM-1504** asks for MFA for all human users of online services and names the factors, not the policy design. That is CIS.M365.5.2.2.2.
- **ISM-1872** applies to privileged and unprivileged users alike. The Blueprint meets it with one policy for all users and all resources that requires the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength. That is CISA.MS.AAD.3.1.
- **ISM-1649**: the assessment guide describes just-in-time as access granted "immediately before that access is required and for only as long as it is required". The Blueprint makes every Entra role eligible-only, with permanent active assignments only for break glass accounts. That is CIS.M365.5.3.1. The earlier check failed only permanent assignments, so a six-month active assignment passed.
- **ISM-1403** is CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 with a maximum of 5 instead of 10. The Blueprint also sets 5.

**Shims.** Those four tests are now shims. Each has its own ID, title, `Control` and guide, and its body returns the other test's result, e.g. `return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser` or `return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`. Each ASD requirement keeps its own row, with its maturity level, and there's one implementation per setting. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` finds every shim and fails when:

- its attributes differ from the test it calls;
- it calls a test that doesn't exist, or that is itself a shim;
- it passes a parameter that test doesn't declare;
- its requirement is also on that test's `Control`;
- its guide doesn't name that test.

The rule is now written down for future tests, under [Tests that another suite already has](https://maester.dev/docs/next/writing-tests#tests-that-another-suite-already-has), in `contributing.md`, in `AGENTS.md` ("Reviewing a test for duplicates") and in the maester-test-expert skill and agents.

**Removed and renamed**

- **ASD.ISM-1173 is removed.** ASD assesses ISM-1173 and ISM-0974 by watching a sign-in to a workstation, not to an online service. MFA for admins in online services is covered by ISM-1504 and ISM-1872, which apply to all users.
- **ASD.ISM-0445 is now ASD.ISM-1175.** The assessment guide tests ISM-1175 by listing the privileged accounts that have an email address, which is what this check does. ISM-0445 stays as its second `Control`.
- **CIS.M365.5.3.1 and 5.3.3 are back to `main`.** The ISM-1649 requirement now lives on the shim. CIS 5.3.3 requires weekly or monthly access reviews where ISM-1647 allows 12 months, so a CIS failure doesn't mean ISM-1647 fails.
- **`Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` is removed.** It repeated MT.1006 and MT.1007.
- **`Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` is now `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser`**, in `internal/services/entra`. It also counts members of role-assignable groups, so an admin who holds a role through a group is no longer missed. It reads the privileged roles with the same beta `$filter=isPrivileged eq true` call as CIS 5.3.1, because `$select=isPrivileged` on v1.0 returns 400 (MT.1209 notes this). ISM-1648 and the mailbox check would have errored on that call.
- **ASR:** reading the rules moved to `Get-MtIntuneAsrRule` in `internal/services/intune`, so MT.1178 can use it later. `Test-MtAsdAsrRule` now takes several rules.

**Fixes from ASD's assessment guide**

- **ISM-1667** also needs *Block Office communication application from creating child processes* (`26190899-…`). The guide lists both rules.
- **ISM-1668** also needs *Block executable content from email client and webmail* (`BE9BA2D9-…`).
- **ISM-1672** now needs Macro Runtime Scan Scope set to all documents. ASD's [macro guide](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/restricting-microsoft-office-macros) and the Blueprint both set that. The low-trust scope scans only files with the Mark of the Web, whose macros ISM-1488 already blocks.
- **ISM-1654:** the Blueprint removes IE11 with a platform script, which Maester can't read, so a Blueprint tenant fails this check. The result and the guide now say so, and explain how to turn the test off with a reason.
- **ISM-1648:** Severity and ImplementationCost are now Medium, as the attribute review asked.
- **CISA.MS.AAD.3.1** now matches the built-in strength by ID, and accepts a custom strength limited to Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 and certificate-based MFA, as ScubaGear does. Before, any custom strength named "Phishing-resistant MFA" passed, whatever methods it allowed.

**Also:**

- Merged `main` and reverted the generated `Invoke-Maester.mdx`.
- Regenerated the test builder and golden data.
- Updated the titles to the September 2026 ISM wording ("human users").
- Added `AsdChecks.Tests.ps1`, which mocks Graph and covers the changed logic.
- Added a `suite: asd` label.

Two things for you:

1. **A tenant run.** The three Graph behaviours you flagged still need one: `signInActivity` inside the `$batch` (ISM-1648), `$expand=assignments` on `configurationPolicies`, and the `isof()` filter on `deviceConfigurations` (ISM-1695). Could you run `Invoke-Maester -Suite asd` against a tenant and post the results?
2. **The PR description.** It still lists 15 checks with ISM-1173 and ISM-0445. It's now 14, and ISM-0445 is ISM-1175.

The refactor and the new guidance are done locally on the #2552 branch. Nothing is committed or pushed yet. The full unit test run is still going, and I'll commit and push once it passes.

**The ASD tests**
- **Four are now shims** that return another suite's result:
  - ISM-1504 runs CIS 5.2.2.2.
  - ISM-1872 runs CISA 3.1.
  - ISM-1649 runs CIS 5.3.1.
  - ISM-1403 runs CIS 5.2.3.8 with a maximum of 5.
- **Dropped or renamed:** ISM-1173 is gone. ISM-0445 is now ISM-1175. CIS 5.3.1 and 5.3.3 are back to `main`, since the shims now carry the ASD requirements.
- **Helpers:** `Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` is gone. `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` is now the general `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser` in `internal/services/entra`, and it also counts admins who get their role through a group. Reading the ASR rules moved to `services/intune`.
- **A real bug I found along the way:** the old privileged-user helper selected `isPrivileged` on Graph v1.0, which Graph rejects with a 400. ISM-1648 and the mailbox check would have errored on their first tenant run.
- **Intune fixes against ASD's assessment guide:**
  - ISM-1667 and ISM-1668 now require both rules each.
  - ISM-1672 now requires macro scanning for all documents.
  - ISM-1654: the result now explains that removing Internet Explorer, as ASD's Blueprint does, also meets the control.
- **CISA 3.1** now matches the built-in phishing-resistant strength by ID. Before, a custom strength *named* "Phishing-resistant MFA" passed even if it allowed push notifications.

**The guidance for writing and reviewing tests with agents**
- **`AGENTS.md`** has a new "Reviewing a test for duplicates" step, before the attribute review. It tells an agent to:
  - search every suite for a test that reads the same setting;
  - read the benchmark's own sources (assessment guidance, reference build), not only the requirement's one-line text;
  - write a shim when the benchmark asks for the same thing;
  - fail the review when a test re-implements a check without a reason from those sources, or when a general helper is named after a suite.

  Every coding agent in the repo reads this file.
- **The same rule, with an example,** is in the writing-tests guide ("Tests that another suite already has"), the contributing guide, the attribute rubric, and the test-expert skill and agents. The `.claude` copies are regenerated from those sources.
- **A new unit test, `TestShims.Tests.ps1`,** finds every shim automatically. It fails if a shim's attributes differ from the test it calls, if it calls a missing test or another shim, or if the requirement it implements is also listed on the test it calls. I checked that it catches a changed Severity and a duplicated requirement.

I also added a `suite: asd` label and `AsdChecks.Tests.ps1`, which exercises the changed logic with mocked Graph data. All 14 ASD tests validate with `Get-MtTest`, and nothing has run against a tenant.

- **ISM-1654:** the Blueprint removes IE11 with a platform script, which Maester can't read, so a Blueprint tenant fails this check. The result and the guide now say so, and explain how to turn the test off with a reason.
- **ISM-1648:** Severity and ImplementationCost are now Medium, as the attribute review asked.
- **CISA.MS.AAD.3.1** now matches the built-in strength by ID, and accepts a custom strength limited to Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 and certificate-based MFA, as ScubaGear does. Before, any custom strength named "Phishing-resistant MFA" passed, whatever methods it allowed.

**Also:**

- Merged `main` and reverted the generated `Invoke-Maester.mdx`.
- Regenerated the test builder and golden data.
- Updated the titles to the September 2026 ISM wording ("human users").
- Added `AsdChecks.Tests.ps1`, which mocks Graph and covers the changed logic.
- Added a `suite: asd` label.

Two things for you:

1. **A tenant run.** The three Graph behaviours you flagged still need one: `signInActivity` inside the `$batch` (ISM-1648), `$expand=assignments` on `configurationPolicies`, and the `isof()` filter on `deviceConfigurations` (ISM-1695). Could you run `Invoke-Maester -Suite asd` against a tenant and post the results?
2. **The PR description.** It still lists 15 checks with ISM-1173 and ISM-0445. It's now 14, and ISM-0445 is ISM-1175.
